title: Strong shapes: triangles
examples: Teacher, why are triangles better than squares for bridges?
Can you show me how a triangle keeps things from falling down?
What other shapes are strong like triangles?

explain.say: Today you will learn why triangles are strong shapes.
Now look. This is a truss bridge in 3D. Can you see the top chord and the bottom chord? Tap any part to hear about it.
A triangle has three straight sides and three corners.
Push on the corner of a square frame. It can lean and change shape.
Triangles keep their shape when you push them.
That is why engineers use triangles in bridges and towers.
Look at a playground slide. Its supports often make triangles.

faq.q: Why do triangles keep things from falling down?
faq.a: Each side of a triangle holds the other two in place. So the shape stays firm unless a side breaks.
asks: What shape is best for building?

faq.a: No. The size of a triangle and what it is made of change how strong it is.
asks: Does the size change the strength?
Are there different kinds of strong triangles?

faq.q: Do we use triangles in buildings all the time?
faq.a: Yes. Engineers use triangles in bridges, towers and roofs.
asks: Can a square ever be as strong as a triangle?
Is this only for big buildings?

faq.q: What is the difference between a triangle and a square?
faq.a: A square has four sides and four corners. A triangle has three sides and three corners.
asks: How many corners does a triangle have?
Which shape is better for building?

faq.q: Does the angle size matter for strength?
faq.a: Yes. The angles change how the push spreads along the sides.
asks: How do angles affect the shape?
Must the angles add up to 180?

facts: A triangle has exactly three sides and three corners.
Triangles are very strong shapes that do not easily change their shape when pushed.
Engineers use triangles in bridges and towers to make them stable.
A square can wobble or collapse more easily than a triangle under force.

quiz.say: Which shape keeps a frame strongest when you push it?
quiz.why: A triangle keeps its shape, so the frame stays strong.

wrong.0: A square frame can lean when you push a corner.
wrong.2: A rectangle frame can lean, just like a square.

quiz.say: Why do bridges have lots of triangles?
quiz.why: Triangles keep their shape, so the bridge stays strong.

wrong.1: Triangles can look nice, but they are there to make the bridge strong.
wrong.2: Triangles stop bending, so the bridge stays firm.

quiz.say: Push on the corner of a square frame. What happens?
quiz.why: A square can lean into a squashed shape. A triangle would stay firm.

wrong.0: A square frame can lean, so its shape changes.
wrong.1: The sides stay straight, so it leans but keeps four sides.
